about: The travellers at a generated country's inns who would go along with a company (src/world/region-recruits.ts): each settlement's traveller follows one of these callings, which is a class (a drover can fight, a pilgrim pray, a tinker open locks), and says what brings them there when asked; near: the classes one turns to whose people cannot take the calling's own (a halfling scholar a bard, not a warrior: PT-13); passing: what one with no calling here says; hire: what the company knows of the inn's traveller from the first ({town}, {one}: the traveller, or 'a traveller'; {country}); hiring: what the innkeeper says while the traveller waits ({traveller} and {keeper} are the world's names for them).

drover.brings: Took a drove over the hills and came back with nothing but blisters and the price of a bed.

tinker.brings: Mending pots. There are more locks than pots in this country, and they pay better.

pilgrim.brings: I walk from shrine to shrine. The gods have not said where to stop.

pedlar.brings: Ribbons, pins and news. The news sells best.

charcoal-burner.brings: The burn is done and the charcoal sold. I have a month before the next.

eel-catcher.brings: The eels are not running. Nothing is, this season.

trapper.brings: The furs are sold, and the snow is late.

minstrel.brings: Playing for my supper. The suppers have been thin, this side of the hills.

scholar.brings: Copying the old inscriptions, for a library that may not want them. It is the copying I like.

soldier.brings: My company was paid off at midsummer. I have a sword, a bad knee and no reason to be anywhere.

mason.brings: Walls. There is always somebody whose wall has fallen down, and they always want it by market day.

hire: At the inn at {town}, {one} is looking for work, and would come with you for a few coins and their keep; the inns of {country}'s other towns have others.
hiring: '{traveller} there is looking for work,' says {keeper}. 'Would go anywhere with anyone, for a few coins and their keep.'
